classification.difficultyReason: In the hardest parts, distinguish diagonal, lateral edge and perpendicular height, derive the base side, then select a second right triangle to obtain face height before summing areas.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of each of these square-based pyramids:

spec.description: Square-based right pyramid with a labelled face slant height from the apex to the midpoint of the right base edge. Decorative orange fill omitted; concealed edges dashed.
spec.mathematics: Base side 6 cm; face slant height 6 cm.

spec.description: Square-based right pyramid with face slant height ending at the midpoint of the right base edge. Decorative fill omitted; concealed edges dashed.
spec.mathematics: Base side 4 m; face slant height 6 m.

spec.description: Square-based right pyramid with interior perpendicular height terminating at the base centre. Interior measurement retained as a construction line; decorative fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Base side 6 cm; perpendicular height 4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived slant height is supplied.

answer.short:
$96\,\mathrm{cm}^2$

Use Pythagoras to find the face slant height, $5\,\mathrm{cm}$.
answer.worked:
Let $l$ be the face slant height in centimetres. The distance from the base centre to an edge midpoint is $3\,\mathrm{cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}l&=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}\\l&=5\\A&=6^2+4\left(\frac12\times6\times5\right)\\A&=36+60\\A&=96\,\mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Square-based right pyramid with interior perpendicular height terminating at the base centre. Decorative fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Base side 2 m; perpendicular height 3 m.

answer.short:
$(4+4\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{m}^2$

The face slant height is $\sqrt{10}\,\mathrm{m}$ by Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
Let $l$ be the face slant height in metres. The distance from the base centre to an edge midpoint is $1\,\mathrm{m}$.
$$\begin{align*}l&=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}\\l&=\sqrt{10}\\A&=2^2+4\left(\frac12\times2\times\sqrt{10}\right)\\A&=(4+4\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: The 8 cm segment joins opposite base vertices; the 6 cm label belongs to a lateral edge from apex to base vertex. Decorative fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Base diagonal 8 cm; lateral edge 6 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither base side nor face slant height is supplied.

answer.short:
$(32+16\sqrt{14})\,\mathrm{cm}^2$

Find the base side from its diagonal, then the face slant height by Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the base side and $l$ the face slant height, in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}2s^2&=8^2\\s^2&=32\\s&=4\sqrt2\\l&=\sqrt{6^2-(2\sqrt2)^2}\\l&=2\sqrt7\\A&=32+4\left(\frac12\times4\sqrt2\times2\sqrt7\right)\\A&=(32+16\sqrt{14})\,\mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two distinct interior segments: perpendicular apex-to-centre height and base-centre-to-vertex half-diagonal, each labelled 4 m. Decorative fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular height 4 m; half base diagonal 4 m.
spec.answerVisibility: No base side or face slant height is supplied.

answer.short:
$(32+32\sqrt3)\,\mathrm{m}^2$

Double the centre-to-vertex length to obtain the base diagonal, then use Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
The base diagonal is $8\,\mathrm{m}$. Let $s$ be the base side and $l$ the face slant height, in metres.
$$\begin{align*}2s^2&=8^2\\s^2&=32\\s&=4\sqrt2\\l&=\sqrt{4^2+(2\sqrt2)^2}\\l&=2\sqrt6\\A&=32+4\left(\frac12\times4\sqrt2\times2\sqrt6\right)\\A&=(32+32\sqrt3)\,\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$
